# Web authority signing vectors

These test-only, fabricated identities exercise protocol 10 / state version 3.
The shared Go/Android vectors in `internal/deviceauth/testdata` and
`internal/e2e/testdata` are unchanged.

From the repository root, regenerate with:

```sh
go run ./web/src/testdata/authority/go > web/src/testdata/authority/vectors.json
```

`web/src/authority.test.ts` regenerates and compares the committed vector, then
builds the same states in TS with fixed keys, times, HPKE input keying material
(`0x71` repeated 32 times), PrevSecret nonce (`0x72` repeated 12 times), recovery
nonce (`0x73` repeated 32 times), and approval nonce (`0x74` repeated 16 times).
It compares the full serialized states, leases, recovery statement, normal and
machine-replacement approvals, and signatures byte for byte. `membership` and
`remove` deliberately produce the same vector. Clock rollback is exercised by
`rotateX`, `veto`, and `recovery`; the lease also exercises a persisted time floor.

The Go oracle calls production Go state builders for the cores. It substitutes
fixed encryption randomness, then uses the Go state serializer and Ed25519 to
sign. Go's `crypto/hpke.NewSender` does not accept deterministic randomness, so
only this test helper implements the RFC 9180 base-mode sender key schedule
with standard Go ECDH, HKDF and AES-GCM; DHKEM key derivation still uses
`crypto/hpke`. Every generated grant is independently opened by production
`deviceauth.Pin.OpenGrant` (which uses `crypto/hpke`). Production crypto and
random sources are not changed.

For the reverse direction the test sends the **TS-generated bytes** to:

```sh
go run ./web/src/testdata/authority/go verify < ts-output.json
```

The helper parses and canonically reserializes states, verifies the genesis and
every transition with `Pin.VerifyGenesis` / `VerifyTransition`, checks recovery
and both leases, verifies both approvals with `e2e.VerifyPairApproval`, opens
every recipient grant, and checks every PrevSecret. TS signs using
nonextractable WebCrypto Ed25519 keys. A tampered certificate must be rejected
by the Go verifier. This is a core interoperability test; it is not a browser,
server/daemon/real-CLI end-to-end test.

Behavior references (line numbers refer to the batch-A baseline):

| TS builder / primitive | Android core | Go |
|---|---|---|
| `Authority.genesis` | `Authority.kt:58` | `state.go:543 BuildGenesis` |
| `Authority.membership` | `Authority.kt:85` | `pair.go:45 BuildMembershipState`, `state.go:551 BuildState` |
| `Authority.pair` | `Authority.kt:100` | `pair.go:58 BuildPairState` |
| `Authority.remove` | `Authority.kt:121` | `BuildMembershipState`, `state.go:454 membershipDelta` |
| `Authority.rotateX` | `Authority.kt:139` | `BuildMembershipState`, `membershipDelta` |
| `Authority.veto` | `Authority.kt:159` | `state.go:580 BuildRecoveryKeyRotation` |
| `Authority.handoff` | `Authority.kt:185` | `lease.go:119 BuildHandoff` |
| `Authority.recovery` | `Authority.kt:218` | `recovery.go:134 BuildRecovery` |
| `sealGrant` / `sealPrevSecret` | `DeviceSecurity.kt:468 / :492` | `state.go:498 sealHPKE / :641 sealPrevSecret` |
| `RecoveryCode` / `signRecoveryStatement` | `Recovery.kt:15`, `DeviceSecurity.kt:993` | `recovery.go:104 RecoveryStatement.Sign` (code encoding is Android's format) |
| `HeadLease.sign` / `signLease` | `Lease.kt:68` | `lease.go:66 BuildLease` |
| `makePairApproval` | `Approval.kt:17`, `PairFlow.kt:274` | `internal/e2e/approval.go:25 NewPairApprovalReplacing` |
| Signing time / renewal | `DeviceSecurity.kt:1056`, `Authority.kt:27` | `BuildLease` plus caller's persisted floor |
| Local creation / recovery public intake | `Authority.kt:372`, `Recovery.kt:91` | account ID derivation and the existing chain verifiers |

Android paths are relative to `android/core/src/main/kotlin/io/github/lewin671/remoteagent/core`;
Go state paths are relative to `internal/deviceauth` unless qualified.

`account-public.test.ts` covers validated public-key intake for local creation,
paired registration (including network interruption and retry), and recovery
context (offline genesis prefix, full chain and local pin/extension). Only a
separate public profile is written; the existing account, registration-intent
and security-record formats remain unchanged. The creation factory and
recovery-context intake do not submit or publish anything. Pending operations,
foreground locks, UI, network recovery orchestration, and real CLI acceptance
belong to later batches.
